answers.explanation: Most are hybrids that combine several approaches.
Each pure model is weak somewhere; mixing lets a system get the strengths of several.
One kernel address space for speed, with loadable modules.
Subsystem personalities let it support different APIs.
Aqua is the GUI; Cocoa is the programming environment.
Cocoa sits in the application-environments layer.
Mach plus BSD, plus the I/O kit and kernel extensions.
That's what makes it a hybrid: microkernel roots, monolithic speed.
